newsitem.title: CANADA: AIDS sufferer wins millions in Quebec lottery.
newsitem.headline: AIDS sufferer wins millions in Quebec lottery.

text.p: A woman who had to pinch pennies to pay for her AIDS medication won C$10 million (U.S. $7.3 million) on Friday and planned to go to the United States to seek medical help for her disease, a news agency said.
Antionette Distilio, a 51-year-old resident of a Montreal AIDS hospice, won the first Lotto 6-49 draw of the new year.
"I've never been lucky," Canadian Press quoted Distilio as saying.

The former clerk in a financial institution, who quit her job in 1991 to care for her health after she was confirmed to be HIV positive, wavered between happiness and tears at a news conference at the Loto-Quebec headquarters.
She said she would share her winnings with friends and family, as well as an anti-AIDS foundation.
"I'm looking forward to a much better quality of life, for me and my friends. For how long, I don't know. I also always want to stay who I am," Distilio told reporters.
Canadian Press said Distilio, who bought lottery tickets only occasionally, bought the winning ticket on New Year's Day after missing the bus to her bingo game.
"So instead of playing bingo I went into the grocery store and bought one ticket," she said.
